items.claim: The opening at 15:5 is grounded in an explicit addressee shift to Jerusalem, and this unit correctly holds 15:5-9 together across its internal alternation between direct address and third-person description.
items.evidence: 15:5 turns from the third-person report to Jeremiah about "this people" and Manasseh (15:1-4) to a second-feminine-singular apostrophe naming Jerusalem directly, כִּ֠י מִֽי יַחְמֹ֤ל עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (byte tier, oshb:Jer.15.5); the poem then alternates between that direct address (15:5-6) and third-person description of the widows and the destroyer (15:7-9) with the same speaker and topic across 15:5-9, so no tier-1 marker intervenes to force an internal cut. This unit closes on the neum-YHWH formula, נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte tier, oshb:Jer.15.9), which properly corroborates the close since a fresh speaker change to Jeremiah's own outcry follows immediately at 15:10.

items.claim: The span 15:10-21 correctly holds together as the confession-dialogue unit, and its two internal onsets are properly read as continuing the same frame-owner rather than opening fresh rows.
items.evidence: 15:10 opens on the oy-apostrophe lexeme, אֽוֹי לִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֣י יְלִדְתִּ֗נִי (byte tier, oshb:Jer.15.10), one of 8 verse-wide occurrences of that distinct lexeme (sweep: 8 verses; oshb:Jer.4.13, Jer.4.31, Jer.6.4, Jer.10.19, Jer.13.27, Jer.15.10, Jer.45.3, Jer.48.46), here marking Jeremiah's own outcry against the divine judgment speech that had just closed at 15:9 -- a genuine speaker change licensing the fresh unit. Yahweh's reply opens at 15:11 without any further addressee change, and the second onset at 15:19, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (byte tier, oshb:Jer.15.19), is koh-amar without a frame-owner change -- the same Jeremiah-Yahweh dialogue pair continues through the deliverance promise at 15:21, so neither internal onset opens a fresh row.

items.claim: 16:1 opens a genuine word-event unit, and the three prohibitions it gathers correctly stay one row because all three koh-amar onsets inside the span (16:3, 16:5, 16:9) explain the command just given without changing the frame-owner.
items.evidence: 16:1 opens וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.1), one of 21 vayehi-debar-YHWH word-event verses book-wide (sweep: 21 verses). The marriage prohibition at 16:2, לֹֽא תִקַּ֥ח לְךָ֖ אִשָּׁ֑ה, is grounded by its own koh-amar onset at 16:3, כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.3); the mourning prohibition at 16:5 opens with the matching koh-amar formula, כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.5); and the feasting prohibition at 16:8 is grounded by the full stacked title at 16:9, כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.9). All three koh-amar onsets keep Yahweh speaking to the same addressee, Jeremiah, about the commands just issued, with no change of frame-owner, so none opens a fresh row; no compliance clause is narrated anywhere in the span, correctly ruling out a symbolic-act reading in favor of judgment content.

items.claim: 16:10 correctly opens a fresh unit on a discourse-frame imperative rather than continuing the prohibitions just closed, and the span correctly holds together as one question-and-answer through 16:13.
items.evidence: 16:10 turns to a conditional report of a coming public question, וְהָיָ֗ה כִּ֤י תַגִּיד֙ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.10), and 16:11 supplies the answer's own discourse-frame imperative, וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.11), matching the book's other imperative-onset seams (compare the declare-and-blow imperative at 4:5 and the hear-the-word imperative at 10:1). The scripted answer runs through the exile sentence at 16:13 as one reply addressed to the wider people, distinct from the personal prohibitions of 16:1-9.

items.claim: The opening at 16:14 has no seam from any of the six ruled tier-1 classes; the cut is driven by the neum-YHWH tag inside its own onset, which is closure corroboration and not a licensed boundary driver.
items.evidence: 16:14 opens לָכֵ֛ן הִנֵּֽה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.14) -- not a vayehi/hadavar/asher-hayah word-event shape, not koh-amar, not a discourse imperative, not a date onset, and not a vision opening. Of those six classes, none is present at 16:14; the neum-YHWH tag inside that same clause is the single formal marker there, functioning per the ruled policy as closure corroboration rather than as an onset driver. No addressee shift accompanies the cut: both 16:10-13 and 16:14-15 describe "them"/"their fathers" in the third person with no new addressee named. The same hinneh-...-neum-YHWH shape recurs byte-for-byte at 16:16, and the whole "days are coming ... neum YHWH" clause recurs a second time at oshb:Jer.23.7 (two further sites, byte tier), marking it as a floating formulaic tag rather than a structural macro-seam device. Reading 16:14-15 as continuing the reply begun at 16:10 is the better-warranted seam on the bytes; confidence is nonetheless rated high over this unsupported driver.
tier_citations: policy: neum-YHWH is closure corroboration, not an onset driver

items.claim: The opening at 16:16 names no seam from any of the six ruled tier-1 classes; the cut from 16:14-15 rests on a change of imagery alone, with no addressee or grammatical-person shift to ground it.
items.evidence: 16:16 opens הִנְנִ֨י שֹׁלֵ֜חַ ... נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה וְדִיג֑וּם (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.16) -- the identical hinneh-plus-participle-plus-neum-YHWH shape as 16:14, and none of the six ruled tier-1 seam classes (word-event, koh-amar with a frame-owner change, addressee/scene shift, discourse imperative, date onset, vision opening) is present at the cut. No addressee or grammatical-person shift separates 16:14-15 from 16:16-18: both use third-person plural object suffixes for the same exiled people (compare the 16:15 "return-them" verb inside וַהֲשִֽׁבֹתִים֙ עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לַאֲבוֹתָֽם with the 16:16 "fish-them" verb inside נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה וְדִיג֑וּם). The fishermen-and-hunters imagery is a real change of topic, but topic change alone is not a licensed driver; the harder question of continuity with 16:14-15 is not engaged; instead, the comparison tested is the more distant and easily-rejected pairing with the trust-hymn at 16:19-21.
tier_citations: policy: tier-1 granularity (six ruled classes; none present at 16:16)

items.claim: 16:19 correctly opens a fresh unit on a genuine speaker and addressee change, and the mixed praise-plus-oracle content is properly typed as doxology against its live judgment-oracle rival.
items.evidence: 16:19 turns from Yahweh's own voice in the pursuit oracle just closed to Jeremiah's direct praise-address to Yahweh, יְהוָ֞ה עֻזִּ֧י וּמָעֻזִּ֛י וּמְנוּסִ֖י בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.19) -- a genuine speaker and addressee change (a human voice addressing the divine, against the divine voice of 16:16-18 describing "them" in the third person). The nations' anticipated confession (16:19-20) and Yahweh's reply closing the unit, וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי שְׁמִ֥י יְהוָֽה (byte tier, oshb:Jer.16.21), read as vindication recognized after that confession rather than a fresh threat, correctly weighing against the judgment-oracle rival considered for 16:21 alone.

items.claim: 17:1 correctly opens a fresh unit on an addressee shift back to third-person indictment of Judah, closing the span at 17:4 on the fire-in-my-anger judgment formula.
items.evidence: 17:1 turns from the trust-hymn's direct address to Yahweh (16:19-21) to third-person description of Judah's sin and altars, חַטַּ֣את יְהוּדָ֗ה כְּתוּבָ֛ה בְּעֵ֥ט בַּרְזֶ֖ל בְּצִפֹּ֣רֶן שָׁמִ֑יר (byte tier, oshb:Jer.17.1) -- a genuine addressee shift matching the book's other addressee-driven seams. The threat of lost treasures and high places (17:3) closes on כִּֽי אֵ֛שׁ קְדַחְתֶּ֥ם בְּאַפִּ֖י עַד עוֹלָ֥ם תּוּקָֽד (byte tier, oshb:Jer.17.4), before a wisdom-style cursed-versus-blessed antithesis opens fresh material at 17:5.
